andrew: Heads up — trying to repro a perf regression in the KV cache path. On long sequences the serving runtime seems to pick a different kernel variant (fp16 fallback?) and latency spikes. Planning an nsys run to get kernel timelines + NVTX brackets. Any preferred flags for batching + KV timeline captures?


tess: Short checklist that has worked for me: trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt for timelines; do one long timeline capture (no sampling) to get exact kernel ordering, then a short sampling capture to surface hotspots. Use capture-range=nvtx to focus on the main request loop. :+1:


ryan: +1 to that. Two tips: 1) make the timeline capture ~60-120s so you capture steady-state batching behaviour (warmup + steady state). 2) avoid too-short sample windows — nsys can miss infrequent kernels if you only capture 5-10s. Also NVTX ranges are lifesavers for zooming.


andrew: Got it. Example commands I'm going to try (feel free to tweak):

```bash
# timeline capture (kernel ordering, KV cache lifetimes)
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o out/kv_timeline --capture-range=nvtx --duration=90 --force-overwrite

# sampling capture (hotspots)
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=cpu,cuda -o out/kv_sampling --capture-range=nvtx --duration=30 --force-overwrite
```


perf-bot: nsys job queued by andrew — remember to attach the .nsys-rep and any extracted timeline screenshots to the thread when done.


sam: A couple more details: set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to isolate the test GPU, and pin the process to a single NUMA node for consistent timing. For the timeline run, use `--sample=none` (same as not specifying sampling in some nsys versions) so file size stays manageable.


julia: NVTX snippet if you want tight brackets around the batch loop (py example):

```python
import nvtx
with nvtx.annotate("serve.batch", color="blue"):
    for batch in batches:
        process(batch)
```

This lets you jump directly to the request handling loop in the timeline. Also add small NVTX pushes around KV cache operations (e.g., kv.load, kv.evict) so you can see cache activity relative to kernels.


ryan: One more gotcha: if you're testing quantized kernels, run with `TF_FORCE_GPU_ALLOW_GROWTH`/equivalent to avoid weird allocation noise, and keep the model pinned to the same kernel selection by fixing batch/seq shapes — variable shapes can flip kernels mid-run.


andrew: Running the timeline now (90s). Will upload .nsys-rep to s3 and post link. If anyone wants to watch, I'll stream the rep file load in perf-lab at end. :eyes:

julia: Nice — once you have the timeline, check kernels that follow kv.load NVTX ranges. If you see repeated small kernels back-to-back, that's a good sign batching heuristics are splitting the work; we might need to adjust the batch coalescing threshold.


andrew: Will dig in and report hotspots. Thanks for the quick tips everyone.
